app.name: Agent Hub
common.copy_failed: Could not copy; select the text and copy it manually
auth.title: API key
auth.explain: The hub asked for a key. Paste an admin or viewer key; it is kept for this browser tab only and never written to disk.
auth.required: Add your API key with the key button in the top bar.
palette.title: Command palette
palette.placeholder: Type to find a page, item or client
err.network: Cannot reach the Agent Hub backend. Check that it is running on 127.0.0.1:8792 and reload.
err.unauthorized: The hub needs an API key. Use the key button in the top bar to add one.
err.csrf: The request was refused because the X-Agent-Hub header was missing. Reload the page; if it persists the frontend and backend versions do not match.
err.forbidden: You do not have permission for this. A viewer key can read but not change content; use an admin key.
err.plan_stale: The content changed after this plan was made, so it can no longer be applied. Create a fresh plan and review it again.
err.conflict: Someone else changed this while you were editing. Reload it to see the latest version, then re-apply your edit.
err.conflict_generic: This conflicts with something that already exists or with the current state.
err.too_large: That is too large for the hub to accept. Split it into smaller pieces.
err.unsupported_media: The hub only accepts JSON. This is a frontend bug; reload the page.
err.bad_host: The hub only answers to localhost or 127.0.0.1. Open it at http://127.0.0.1:8792/ instead of another host name.
err.rate_limited: Too many requests. Wait a few seconds and try again.
err.unavailable: The service is unavailable right now (for example the knowledge service is not running). Start it and try again.
concern.skills_desc: Skill folders copied into the client's skills directory.
concern.agents_desc: Subagent definition files with native tool names.
concern.instructions_desc: A hub-owned block inside the client's instructions file.
concern.mcp_desc: MCP server entries in the client's config file.
concern.permissions_desc: Allow, ask and deny rules and egress settings.
rule.match_hint_tool: A capability name such as shell, web_fetch or edit.
rule.match_hint_command: A command pattern such as rm -rf * (glob).
rule.match_hint_egress_host: A host name such as pypi.org (glob).
rule.sentence: When the agent tries something, what should happen?
rule.reason_hint: Shown to whoever reviews this rule later.
rule.floor_hint: These come from the policy floor and cannot be changed here. A rule you write may only be stricter than these.
rule.floor_violation: This would weaken the policy floor:
rules.locked_why: Locked by the policy floor: it can be made stricter but never weaker from this screen.
lib.title: Library
lib.search_ph: Search by name, description or tag
lib.enable_hint: Pick the clients that should get the selected items. Clients that cannot use an item are skipped and reported.
lib.disable_hint: Pick the clients that should stop using the selected items.
lib.enable_done: {changed} change(s) written, {skipped} skipped. Review them under Changes.
lib.empty_hint: Start by importing the skills, agents and instructions your clients already have, or create a first item.
lib.none_hint: Try a shorter search or clear the filters.
new.title: Title
new.title_ph: What is it called in plain words?
new.name: Identifier
new.name_hint: Lowercase letters, digits, dot, dash and underscore. It becomes the file name and cannot be changed later.
new.bad_name: Use 1 to 64 characters: lowercase letters, digits, dot, dash or underscore, starting with a letter or digit.
picker.hint_multi: Tick every collection this belongs in. An item can be in several.
picker.none: There are no collections yet. Create one first.
coll.title: Collections
coll.intro: Collections group things that belong together. Enable a whole collection for a client in one click; an item can live in several collections.
coll.dnd_hint: Drag items onto a collection, or drag collections to reorder. Prefer the keyboard? Use the Move buttons and the Move to collection button on each item.
coll.move_selected: Move ticked items to a collection
coll.none_hint: Create your first collection, for example "Everyday coding", then drag items into it.
coll.drop_here: Drop items here to add them.
coll.loose_one: {count} item is not in any collection
coll.loose_other: {count} items are not in any collection
coll.all_grouped: Every item is in at least one collection.
coll.select_first: Tick at least one item first.
coll.missing_hint: It may have been deleted. Pick one from the list.
coll.reorder_hint: Drag rows to reorder, or use the arrow buttons.
coll.empty_hint: Add items below, or drag them here from the library.
coll.everything_in: Everything is already in this collection.
coll.enable_hint: Tick a client to give it everything in this collection. Items a client cannot use are skipped and explained in the plan.
coll.delete_confirm: Delete the collection "{name}"? The items in it are not deleted, but clients that got them only through this collection will lose them.
coll.f_id_hint: Used in file names. Lowercase letters, digits, dot, dash, underscore.
coll.w_desc_ph: What belongs here and who it is for
coll.w_id_taken: A collection with that identifier already exists.
coll.w_items_hint: Tick anything to start with. You can add more later.
coll.w_enable: Enable it for these clients right away
mx.title: Matrix
mx.table_label: Which item is enabled for which client
mx.via_hint: Enabled through a collection. Switching it off here adds an override for this client only.
mx.nothing_toggleable: Nothing here can be switched: the cells are blocked or not supported.
mx.unsaved_detail: {on} on, {off} off. Nothing takes effect until you save, commit, plan and apply.
mx.saved_one: Saved {count} change to the working tree.
mx.saved_other: Saved {count} changes to the working tree.
mx.empty_title: There is nothing to show yet
mx.empty_hint: Import or create some items and add a client; they will appear here.
editor.delete_confirm: Delete {name}? It is removed from every collection and profile. You can still get it back from history until you commit.
editor.name: Identifier
editor.name_fixed: The identifier is the folder name and cannot be changed. Duplicate the item to get a different one.
editor.name_fixed_new: This becomes the file name once you save.
editor.title: Title
editor.skill_desc: Description (when should an agent use this?)
editor.skill_desc_hint: Agents read this line to decide whether to load the skill, so say when it applies.
editor.frontmatter_hint: This header is generated from the fields and put at the top of SKILL.md.
editor.file_hint: Relative to the skill folder, for example references/notes.md. No .., no leading slash.
editor.tags_ph: Type a tag and press Enter
editor.notes_hint: For you only. Never delivered to a client.
editor.capabilities_hint: Tick capabilities in plain words; the hub maps each to the client's real tool name.
editor.mapping: What each client will call these
editor.mapping_hint: A dash means the client has no native tool for that capability.
editor.agents_unsupported: This client does not load subagent files.
editor.tier_hint: Each client maps fast, standard and deep to a concrete model.
editor.read_only: Read-only: this agent must not change files
editor.applies_hint: Leave all unticked to apply to every client.
editor.order_hint: Instructions are joined in this order. Drag rows, or use the arrows.
editor.memory_note: Memories are curated: they only get here by being promoted from the inbox or written by you.
editor.rendered_hint: The exact file content the hub would deliver to this client for this item.
editor.rendered_none: No client can use this kind of item
editor.rendered_none_hint: None of your clients supports it, so there is nothing to render.
editor.rendered_empty_hint: This item is not enabled for that client. Turn it on in the matrix.
editor.merge_tip: How the hub writes this file: own = whole file, block = only its marked block, json_keys / yaml_keys = only its keys
editor.used_hint: Switch this item on or off per client. Changes go to the working tree; nothing is delivered until you apply.
editor.enable_na: This item cannot be enabled per client.
val.name_bad: The identifier must be 1 to 64 characters: lowercase letters, digits, dot, dash, underscore.
val.desc_short: The description is too short ({n} characters; at least {min}). Say when an agent should use it.
val.desc_long: The description is too long (maximum {max} characters).
val.desc_multiline: The description should be a single line; line breaks will be joined.
val.body_frontmatter: The body starts with --- which looks like a second header.
val.agent_no_caps: This agent has no capabilities, so it can do nothing.
val.file_unsafe: The path must be relative and must not contain .. or backslashes.
val.mcp_command: A stdio server needs a command.
val.mcp_url: An http or sse server needs a URL.
val.mcp_wildcard: Wildcard egress (*) is not allowed by the policy floor.
mcp.scan_clean: Scanned clean, pinned at {ref}. It can be enabled for clients.
mcp.scan_findings_hint: The scan found problems. It cannot be enabled for any client until they are fixed and it is rescanned.
mcp.scan_unscanned_hint: This server has not been scanned. It cannot be enabled for any client until a scan comes back clean.
mcp.scan_cmd: Run the scan from the repository root, then reload this page:
mcp.enable_hint: Blocked clients show why. Unsupported ones cannot use this kind of item.
mcp.env_hint: Names only. Values stay with the broker or env file and are never stored in the hub.
mcp.egress_hint: Egress is deny-by-default. List every host this server needs; wildcards are refused.
mcp.pinned_hint: The commit or version that was scanned.
cl.title: Clients
cl.intro: A client is any agent tool the hub delivers content to. Each one shows whether it is in sync, and what it can do right now.
cl.empty_hint: Add the tools you use, such as Claude Code or opencode, or describe a new one with a short spec.
cl.strict_tip: Anything the client cannot do stops an apply.
cl.lenient_tip: Anything the client cannot do is only a warning.
cl.blocked_tip: A floor violation or strict error blocks apply for this client.
cl.drift_summary: {changed} of {total} delivered files differ from what the hub wrote.
cl.drift_missing: The file is missing on disk.
cl.audit_ok: The live configuration meets the policy floor.
cl.audit_bad: The live configuration breaks the policy floor.
cl.delete_confirm: Remove {name} from the hub? Files already delivered to it stay where they are.
cl.effective_intro: Everything below is what {name} gets once the current content is applied.
cl.no_tools: This client does not publish a tool list.
cl.egress_default: by default; only these hosts are reachable:
cl.health_intro: Verify asks the client what it loaded. Drift compares the live files with what the hub last wrote. Audit checks the live config against the policy floor, even for parts the hub does not manage.
cl.manage_intro: The hub only writes what you hand over. Advisory means it shows what it would change and audits the live config, but never writes. Handing over a concern shows the diff first.
cl.concern_unsupported: This client does not support it.
cl.adopt_hint: This is exactly what the next apply would change. Nothing is written until you apply.
cl.unadopt_confirm: Stop managing {concern}? Files stay as they are; the hub will only report differences.
cl.preview_unavailable: The backend cannot preview this yet. You can still adopt it; review the plan before applying.
cl.w_root_hint: Where the client keeps its files. ~ is your home folder.
cl.w_strict: Strict: stop an apply if the client cannot do something
cl.w_strict_hint: Lenient clients only get a warning.
cl.w_review_hint: This is the client that will be added.
cl.w_spec_invalid: Fix the errors in the spec first.
cl.spec_intro: Describe where this client reads skills, instructions and MCP servers. It is checked as you type and a sample is rendered on the right.
cl.spec_hint: YAML or JSON. No code is run.
cl.spec_preview_hint: Files the hub would write with a sample skill and instruction.
spec.code.yaml_syntax: The text is not valid YAML: {message}
spec.code.unsafe_path: {path} must be relative and stay inside the folder.
imp.title: Import
imp.intro: Bring in what your clients already have. Nothing is written to the client; items land in the hub's working tree for you to review.
imp.none_hint: The client has no skills, agents or instructions the hub can read.
imp.c_identical_tip: The hub already has an identical item.
imp.c_different_tip: The hub has an item with this name but different content.
imp.no_conflicts: No conflicts with what the hub already has.
imp.conflicts_hint: These already exist in the hub. Equal ones default to Link; different ones default to Skip so nothing is overwritten. Open Differences to see why they differ.
imp.oc_skip_desc: Skip the item; the hub's copy is unchanged.
imp.oc_rename_desc: Import it under a new name (the name with -2, or the next free number).
imp.oc_replace_desc: Overwrite the hub's copy. You can still undo this from Changes before committing.
imp.preview_summary: {writes} item(s) will be written, {links} linked to existing items, {skip} skipped.
imp.preview_hint: Importing only changes the hub's working tree. You review and commit it under Changes.
chg.title: Changes, plan and apply
chg.intro: Edits change the working tree only. Commit approves the content, a plan shows exactly what each client would get, and apply delivers it.
chg.none_hint: Everything is committed. Edit something, or make a plan to see what each client would get.
chg.commit_hint: A commit records that you approved this content. It is what a plan is built from.
chg.msg_bad: Write a commit message of at least 3 characters.
chg.discard_confirm_one: Discard {count} pending change? This cannot be undone.
chg.discard_confirm_other: Discard {count} pending changes? This cannot be undone.
chg.plan_hint: Pick clients, or leave all unticked to plan for every committed client. Plans are built from committed content and write nothing.
chg.plan_pure: A plan only reads; it changes nothing.
chg.uncommitted_one: {count} uncommitted change is NOT in this plan. Commit it and make a new plan to include it.
chg.uncommitted_other: {count} uncommitted changes are NOT in this plan. Commit them and make a new plan to include them.
chg.apply_blocked_one: {count} client is blocked and will be skipped: {ids}.
chg.apply_blocked_other: {count} clients are blocked and will be skipped: {ids}.
chg.apply_conflicts: {count} file(s) were edited by hand on the client; {adopted} chosen to overwrite. The rest are skipped.
chg.reviewed: I have read the diffs above and want to apply this plan.
chg.apply_confirm: Apply to {clients} client(s), changing {files} file(s)? Backups of overwritten files are kept.
chg.gate_not_reviewed: Tick the box to confirm you reviewed the diffs.
chg.gate_all_blocked: Every client is blocked. Fix the violations first.
chg.gate_no_clients: There are no clients in this plan.
chg.applied_partial: Applied with some clients blocked or files skipped.
chg.revert_confirm: Revert {commit} ("{message}")? This adds a new commit that undoes it; nothing is delivered until you apply.
plan.floor_fix: Fix these in the rules or the matrix, then create a new plan.
plan.blocked_strict: This client is strict and the diagnostics above include errors, so it cannot be applied.
plan.nothing_here: Nothing to show for this client.
plan.conflict_hint: Someone edited this file on the client since the hub last wrote it. By default it is skipped so their edit is kept.
plan.adopt_path: Overwrite their edit with the hub's version
diff.label: Diff: {add} lines added, {del} removed
home.title: Agent Hub
home.intro: One place to organise what every agent client knows and may do. Nothing reaches a client until you review a plan and apply it.
home.step_import_hint: Bring in the skills, agents and instructions your clients already use.
home.step_organise_hint: Group things that belong together, then enable groups per client.
home.step_plan_hint: See exactly what each client would get, file by file.
home.step_apply_hint: Deliver the approved content and verify each client.
inbox.title: Memory inbox
inbox.intro: Agents propose memories here. Nothing becomes a memory until you promote it, because memory is remembered by every future agent.
inbox.empty_hint: When an agent thinks something is worth remembering it will show up here for you to accept or reject.
inbox.promoted: Promoted as {id}. Commit it to make it official.
inbox.suspicious: Looks like an instruction to an agent.
inbox.suspicious_hint: It matches: {reasons}. Memories that tell an agent what to do can be used to hijack it. Reject it unless you wrote or trust it.
inbox.promote_suspicious: This entry looks like an instruction aimed at future agents. Promote it anyway?
inbox.reason_secrets: mentions secrets together with an action
inbox.reason_pipe_shell: pipes a download into a shell
inbox.reason_disable_guard: asks to switch off a safeguard
inbox.reason_standing_order: is a standing order for any request
k.title: Knowledge
k.intro: Vector stores and shared indexes that agents can read through scoped tokens. Untrusted agents only ever get read access to the namespaces you choose.
k.model_hint: Embeddings come from the router. The dimension must match the model.
k.ns_delete_confirm: Delete the namespace {name} and its {count} documents? This cannot be undone.
k.ns_empty_hint: Create a namespace, then ingest documents into it.
k.ing_meta_hint: Stored with the document, for example where it came from.
k.ing_meta_bad: The metadata is not valid JSON.
k.ing_path_hint: Only folders under the allowed roots are accepted; the server refuses others.
k.q_ph: What do you want to find?
k.q_none_hint: Try different words or lower the minimum score.
k.tok_intro: A token lets one client read (or write) chosen namespaces. It is shown once when created and stored hashed. New tokens should stay read-only.
k.mode_write_tip: Can also add and delete documents
k.tok_none_hint: Agents cannot reach the knowledge service until you create a token for them.
k.tok_client_hint: The client name this token is for, for example hermes.
k.tok_scope_hint: Read is the default and the safest choice. Only give write to a client you trust to change this data.
k.tok_revoke_confirm: Revoke the token for {client}? The client loses access immediately.
k.secret_once: Copy this now. It is shown only once and cannot be recovered; if you lose it, create a new one.
k.ix_intro: Shared read-only indexes, such as code graphs, that clients can be pointed at.
k.ix_path_hint: An absolute path or one starting with ~/, without ..
k.ix_none_hint: Register the output folder of a code-graph or symbol indexer so clients can use it.
k.ix_delete_confirm: Remove {name} from the registry? The folder itself is not touched.
set.title: Settings and audit
set.paths_hint: These are fixed at start-up and shown for reference.
set.endpoints_hint: URLs written into client configs, so every client uses the same addresses.
set.secret_keep: Leave empty to keep the current secret
set.secret_tip: A secret is set. Its value is never sent to the browser.
set.secret_hint: Type a new value only to replace it. The stored one is never shown or sent back.
set.keys_intro: Keys give access to this hub. Admin keys can change things; viewer keys can only read.
set.key_delete_confirm: Delete the key {name}? Anything using it stops working.
set.floor_intro: The policy floor is a fixed set of rules in the app repository. Content can be stricter than it but never weaker, and it cannot be edited from here.
app.uninitialised: The content repository has not been initialised, so nothing can be edited yet. Run hubctl init, then reload.
err.cell: That item cannot be enabled for this client right now.
err.never_applied: Nothing has been applied to this client yet. Apply a plan first, then verify.
err.client_not_committed: This client is not in committed content yet. Commit your changes first.
err.content_not_initialised: The content repository is not initialised. Run hubctl init and reload.
err.content_invalid: Some content has validation problems. Fix or discard them before committing.
err.dirty_tree: Commit or discard your pending changes before reverting.
err.exists: Something with that name already exists. Pick another name.
err.confirm: The hub needs an explicit confirmation for this. Use the Apply button.
err.floor_locked: That is part of the policy floor and cannot be changed here.
err.adapter: The adapter for this client is not installed.
err.method: The hub does not allow that operation through its proxy. Use the service's own API or CLI instead.
cl.no_adapter_tip: The adapter this client uses is not installed, so nothing can be rendered for it.
cl.effective_working: This client is not committed yet, so this shows what it would get from your uncommitted changes.
cl.dstate_modified_live_hint: The live file differs from what the hub last wrote.
cl.dstate_missing_hint: The file is missing on disk.
cl.dstate_never_applied_hint: The hub has not written this file yet.
cl.dstate_pending_hint: The hub has a newer version to apply.
cl.dstate_orphaned_hint: The hub wrote this file earlier and no longer wants it.
cl.dstate_changed_live_hint: Someone changed this file since the hub wrote it. Apply will skip it unless you choose to overwrite.
cl.dstate_unmanaged_hint: The hub does not manage this file.
cl.dstate_advisory_hint: The hub only reports on this file.
editor.tag_bad: "{tag}" is not a valid tag. Use lowercase letters, digits, dot, dash or underscore.
editor.tags_hint: Lowercase words like review or docker.
editor.collections_after_save: Collections are applied right after the first save.
editor.binary_note: This skill contains binary files. Their content cannot be edited here, so file changes are switched off to avoid losing them.
editor.rendered_committed: Rendered from committed content. Uncommitted edits show up here after you commit.
editor.rendered_same: This file is already identical on the client; the hub has nothing to write.
editor.rendered_diff: The client already has this file; showing what would change.
imp.enable_after: Also enable the imported items for {client}
chg.next_plan_hint: Plans are built from committed content. Commit these changes and the plan will include them.
floor.why_network: Egress is deny-by-default; content can only add named hosts.
floor.why_paths: Credentials, keys, browser profiles and the hub's own state are off limits to every client.
floor.why_tool: Content may grant at most this decision for the tool.
floor.why_command: An allow rule for commands needs a real pattern, never a catch-all.
floor.why_mcp: Only a clean scan lets an MCP server be enabled.
floor.why_egress: Every host an MCP server reaches needs its own explicit allow rule.
set.trust_warn: Loopback trust is ON: any local process, including an agent with a shell, acts as admin without a key. Turn it off unless you are debugging.
set.range: {name} must be a whole number from {lo} to {hi}.
set.limits_hint: These are the settings the hub lets you change while it runs.
set.f_plan_retention_hint: How many recent plans stay available for apply.
set.f_inbox_max_per_client_hint: Older proposals are refused once a client reaches this.
set.f_inbox_rate_per_min_hint: Rate limit for agents proposing memories.
set.endpoints_where: Endpoint URLs (router, knowledge) live in the content repository's endpoints.yaml, so they are versioned and reviewed like everything else. Edit that file and commit it.
set.key_client_hint: The client id this token belongs to.
set.key_scopes_hint: Comma separated: inbox:write and/or knowledge:read:<namespace>. Leave empty for none.
set.key_need_client: A client token needs a client id.
set.a_hint: Every change made through the API is recorded here. Memory text and knowledge documents are never logged.
cl.preview_uncommitted: The client is not in committed content yet, so there is nothing to preview. Commit it first; you can still adopt now and review the plan later.
sugg.title: Suggested collections
sugg.intro_one: {count} suggestion, based on how your items are named and tagged.
sugg.intro_other: {count} suggestions, based on how your items are named, tagged and where they came from.
imp.ch_link_desc: Use the item the hub already has; enable it for this client.
imp.ch_rename_desc: Import this client's version under a new name.
imp.ch_replace_desc: Overwrite the hub's item with this client's version.
k.down_title: The knowledge service is not running
k.down_hint: Knowledge (vector stores and shared indexes) is a separate process on 127.0.0.1:8795. The hub cannot reach it. Start it in a terminal:
k.down_systemd: or, if you installed the systemd unit from hub/deploy:
err.knowledge_unavailable: The knowledge service is not reachable. Start it (make run-knowledge) and retry.
err.knowledge_unauthorized: The hub is not configured with the knowledge service's admin key. See the setup steps on the Knowledge page.
k.auth_title: The hub needs the knowledge service's admin key
k.auth_hint: The knowledge service is running, but the hub has no key for it, so it cannot list namespaces. This is not your hub API key. Run this once (the key goes into a private file and is never shown):
k.auth_after: The command appends HUB_KNOWLEDGE_TOKEN to ~/.config/agent-hub/env and restarts the hub; then retry.
k.chip_auth_hint: reachable, but the hub has no admin key for it
doc.intro: The doctor checks this machine for things that weaken the hub's protection. Each finding says what is wrong and a fix you can copy and run yourself; the hub never runs fixes for you.
doc.all_ok: Nothing to fix: every check passed.
